children: 我称之为“创造性的神经症”：把自身的强迫冲动和恐惧引向富有成果的产出，这是一种艺术。本书展示了这种艺术在写作上的应用。就本书而言，我那种要在复杂事件中发现或发明简单对称性的强迫冲动，与另一种冲动结合在一起：通过承担一项不那么艰巨的任务，来逃避一项沉重的责任。本书的任何读者都会看出我那种追求秩序与简化的强迫冲动的迹象。不过，第二种冲动还需要稍作解释。过去有许多次，我为了回避正在变得痛苦或困难的其他工作，一头扎进困难的工作里。这一次，我本来已开始与维姆·布洛克曼斯合作，为一部关于欧洲城市与国家互动的论文集征稿，随后却动手写一部极其宏大的书，比较公元1000年以来欧洲若干地区特定城市与特定国家的联结方式。

Creative neurosis, I call it: the art of directing one's compulsions and fears to productive outcomes. This book illustrates its application to writing. In this case, my compulsion to discover or invent simple symmetry in complex events combined with an urge to escape a burdensome responsibility by taking on another task that was not quite as daunting. Any reader of this book will recognize the signs of my compulsion to order and simplify. The second urge, however, takes a little explaining. Many times before I have found myself plunging into difficult work in order to avoid other work that was proving painful or difficult. This time, having started to collaborate with Wim Blockmans in the recruitment of a collection of papers on interactions of cities and states in Europe, I began an extremely ambitious book comparing the articulation of particular cities and states in several parts of Europe since AD 1000.

我希望这本书能充分回应佩里·安德森提出的重大挑战：“今天，当‘自下而上的历史’在马克思主义和非马克思主义圈子里都成为口号，并极大地增进了我们对过去的理解时，仍然有必要回顾历史唯物主义的一条基本原理：只要阶级还存在，阶级之间绵延已久的斗争最终是在社会的政治层面——而不是经济或文化层面——得到解决的。换言之，正是国家的建构与毁灭，决定了生产关系基本转变的实现。”（Anderson 1974: 11）我希望这本书能把贯穿我学术生涯的三个关切融合起来：集体行动的历史与动力、城市化进程，以及民族国家的形成。

I meant the book to respond adequately to Perry Anderson's great challenge: "Today, when 'history from below' has become a watchword in both Marxist and non-Marxist circles, and has produced major gains in our understanding of the past, it is nevertheless necessary to recall one of the basic axioms of historical materialism: that secular struggle between classes is ultimately resolved at the
political

- not at the economic or cultural - level of society. In other words, it is the construction and destruction of States which seal the basic shifts in the relations of production, so long as classes subsist" (Anderson 1974: 11). The book, I hoped, would merge three of my career-long concerns: the history and dynamics of collective action, the process of urbanization, and the formation of national states.
据我的理解，这样一本书需要精通冷僻的史料和语言，更不用说还要编纂庞大的目录和统计序列，而这些东西只能一项一项地逐渐到位。我开始写作，但很快就发现自己正在偏僻之处挖掘新材料，并在检验自己学习新语言和重新拾起旧语言的能力。康奈尔大学给了我一次机会，让我以1987年“梅辛杰讲座”的形式试验本书的一些组织性观念；伊萨卡的讨论虽然证明这些观念还相当粗糙，但也使我确信这个题目很重要，值得为之付出长期努力。

Such a book, as I understood it, required a mastery of exotic sources and languages, not to mention the compilation of large catalogs and statistical series that would only fall into place an item at a time. I began writing, but soon found myself digging for new material in obscure places, and testing my ability both to learn new languages and retrieve old ones. Cornell University gave me the chance to try out some of the book's organizing ideas as its Messenger Lectures for 1987; although the discussion in Ithaca proved how ragged those ideas were, it also convinced me that the topic was important, and worth the long effort it would demand.

1988年2月和3月，我在写那本书的同时，在巴黎政治学院做了一系列讲座。（感谢阿兰·朗斯洛和皮埃尔·比恩鲍姆安排这个机会，也感谢克莱门斯·海勒在我逗留巴黎期间通过人文科学之家给予的支持。）我的计划是在讲座间隙到巴黎的档案馆工作。但在系列讲座刚开始不久，我又一次讲了欧洲的城市与国家。当我回想那次演讲引发的热烈提问时，突然意识到自己另有一本书已大体成形：一本比我已经开始撰写的那部著作更提纲挈领、更综合、更简明、也更可行的书。写这本书可以让我体面地——哪怕是暂时地——从那个令人生畏的大项目中脱身。我没有去档案馆，而是待在家里，坐在键盘前，兴奋地敲打起这部新书。我在康奈尔和巴黎政治学院所做讲座的修订稿被纳入计划，因此到3月底我回到纽约时，已经草拟了本书的主要部分。

As I was working on that book in February and March 1988, I gave a series of lectures at the Institut d'Etudes Politiques in Paris. (I am grateful to Alain Lancelot and Pierre Birnbaum for arranging that opportunity, and to Clemens Heller for the support of the Maison des Sciences de l'Homme during my stay in Paris.) My plan was to work in Parisian archives in between the lectures. But early in the series I again lectured on European cities and states. As I reflected on the lively questioning that presentation had provoked, I suddenly realized that I had another book well underway: a much more schematic, synthetic, concise, and feasible book than the one I had already begun. Writing that book would allow me an honorable, if temporary, exit from the formidable big project. Instead of going to the archives, I stayed home at my keyboard and began tapping away excitedly at the new volume. Reworked versions of my Cornell and Institut lectures fitted into the plan, so that when I returned to New York at the end of March I had drafted major chunks of the book.

我放下了其他项目——拉塞尔·塞奇基金会曾慷慨地资助我休假一年从事这些项目——急忙坐到电脑前继续写作。（在那段时间里，波琳·罗思坦和她在拉塞尔·塞奇基金会的助手为图书馆资料提供了不可或缺的、聪明的帮助，卡米尔·耶齐让日常事务变得轻松，埃里克·万纳和彼得·德·亚诺西给予亲切的支持，罗伯特·默顿和维维安娜·泽利泽则鼓励我致力于处理大结构、大过程和大比较。）到1988年7月，一部完整但不均衡的草稿已经开始流传。这份草稿及后续各稿先后以《国家、强制与资本》《银、剑与权杖》以及不那么悦耳但更准确的《强制、资本与欧洲国家》为书名传阅。（本书现在的版本吸收并改编了先前发表的材料：〈1500年以来欧洲国家制造与资本主义的地理〉（“The Geography of European Statemaking and Capitalism Since 1500”），收于尤金·吉诺维斯和伦纳德·霍克伯格编《历史中的地理视角》（Geographic Perspectives in History）（牛津：巴兹尔·布莱克韦尔，1989）；〈当代世界的战争制造者与公民〉（“Warmakers and Citizens in the Contemporary World”）（社会变迁研究中心工作论文第41号，1987）；〈战争如何制造国家，国家又如何制造战争〉（“How War Made States and Vice Versa”）（工作论文第42号，1987）；〈国家、强制与资本〉（“States, Coercion, and Capital”）（工作论文第75号，1988）；以及〈法国的国家与反革命〉（“State and Counterrevolution in France”），《社会研究》（Social Research）56卷（1989），第71—98页。）

Neglecting other projects for which the Russell Sage Foundation had graciously sponsored a year's leave, I rushed to my computer and continued to write. (During that time, Pauline Rothstein and her assistants at Russell Sage provided indispensable, intelligent help with library sources, Camille Yezzi made daily routines easy, Eric Wanner and Peter de Janosi offered genial support, while Robert Merton and Viviana Zelizer encouraged my efforts to deal with big structures, large processes, and huge comparisons.) By July 1988 a complete, if uneven, draft was in circulation. It and successive drafts went the rounds under the titles
States, Coercion, and Capital, Silver, Sword, and Scepter,
and the less mellifluous but more accurate
Coercion, Capital, and European States.

在随后的几个月里，许多朋友和同事阅读或听取了本书的各个片段；我那种要谈论它并不断修改的强迫冲动，使他们非常忙碌。珍妮特·阿布-卢戈德、维姆·布洛克曼斯、布鲁斯·卡罗瑟斯、塞缪尔·克拉克、布莱恩·唐宁、卡门萨·加洛、托瓦尔德·格兰、玛约琳·特·哈特、彼得·卡岑斯坦、安德鲁·柯比、约翰·林恩、佩里·马尔斯，
马尔滕·普拉克、西德尼·塔罗、韦恩·特·布拉克和王国斌给了我一份无法估量的礼物：他们仔细批评了整部手稿的早期草稿；理查德·本塞尔、罗伯特·杰维斯、乔·赫斯本兹和戴维·莱廷则对某些章节提出了尖锐意见。我要衷心感谢阿黛尔·罗特曼就如何表达我的想法提出建议。尼基·阿杜巴以极其细致和聪慧的功夫编辑了手稿。路易丝·蒂利在我写这本书时正忙于完成她自己的著作，但她慷慨地容忍我的痴迷，并提供了战略性建议。

During the ensuing months many friends and colleagues read or heard various segments of the book; my compulsion to talk about it and to revise incessantly kept them very busy. Janet Abu-Lughod, Wim Blockmans, Bruce Carothers, Samuel Clark, Brian Downing, Carmenza Gallo, Thorvald Gran, Marjolein 't Hart, Peter Katzenstein, Andrew Kirby, John Lynn, Perry Mars,

Maarten Prak, Sidney Tarrow, Wayne te Brake, and Bin Wong gave me an inestimable gift: they criticized early drafts of the whole manuscript thoughtfully, while Richard Bensel, Robert Jervis, Jo Husbands, and David Laitin added sharp comments on particular sections. 卑尔根大学、加州大学欧文分校、芝加哥大学、日内瓦大学、莱顿大学和西安大略大学，以及纽约市立大学、哥伦比亚大学、哈佛大学和爱沙尼亚科学院的听众，对分析的部分内容提出了尖锐的问题。新学院大学关于国家形成与集体行动的研究班一再帮助我形成本书的论点。我深深感谢哈里森·怀特及其在哥伦比亚大学社会科学中心的同谋者（尤其是莉萨·安德森、戴维·卡纳丁、马丁·加久洛、丹妮丝·杰克逊、杰拉尔德·马韦尔、萨尔瓦托雷·皮特鲁泽洛、凯特·罗伯茨、埃克托尔·沙米斯、卡迈勒·谢哈迪、杰克·斯奈德、克莱尔·厄尔曼和罗南·范·罗塞姆），他们组织了一次愉快的研讨会，仔细审查本书的草稿章节。这些提供帮助的批评者都没有看过本书当前版本的完整草稿，因此都不必为我的错误负责。

Audiences at the Universities of Bergen, California-Irvine, Chicago, Geneva, Leiden, and Western Ontario, at the City University of New York, Columbia University, Harvard University, and the Estonian Academy of Sciences asked pointed questions about parts of the analysis. The New School's proseminar on state formation and collective action helped me repeatedly in formulating the book's arguments. I am deeply indebted to Harrison White and his coconspirators at Columbia University's Center for the Social Sciences (notably Lisa Anderson, David Cannadine, Martin Gargiulo, Denise Jackson, Gerald Marwell, Salvatore Pitruzzello, Kate Roberts, Hector Schamis, Kamal Shehadi, Jack Snyder, Claire Ullman, and Ronan Van Rossem) for a delightful seminar they organized to scrutinize draft chapters from this book. None of these helpful critics has seen a complete draft of the book's current version, and none therefore bears responsibility for my mistakes.

错误肯定不少。跨越一千年，我无疑未能考虑某些重要观念，漏掉了关键事件，忽略了重要矛盾，弄错了一些重要事实，并对某些变化作了错误解释。我只希望读者能告诉我任何错误或遗漏，并且在断然拒绝本书之前，先想一想我的错误在多大程度上影响整体论证。在我乐观的时候，我希望本书能继续已故的斯坦·罗坎所开创的工作，能发扬斯坦和我合作的那部著作《西欧民族国家的形成》的优点并纠正其错误，能体现我在《大结构、大过程、大比较》和《当社会学遇见历史》等早期著作中所倡导的对大规模变迁过程进行有历史根据的研究纲领，并能有助于发展历史偶然性理论——安东尼·吉登斯、艾伦·普雷德、阿瑟·斯廷奇科姆和哈里森·怀特近期的著作就是这种理论的范例。果真如此，强迫冲动和恐惧症就又对知识作出了建设性贡献。当然，现在我面临一个问题：那部大书还在等着我。

Mistakes there surely are. Stretching across a millennium, I have undoubtedly failed to consider major ideas, missed crucial events, ignored important contradictions, gotten significant facts wrong, and explained some changes incorrectly. I hope only that readers will inform me of any errors or omissions, and that they will reflect on how greatly my mistakes affect the overall argument before rejecting it out of hand. In my optimistic moods, I hope that this book will continue the work begun by the late Stein Rokkan, that it will build on the strengths and correct the errors of a work on which Stein and I collaborated,
The Formation of National States in Western Europe,
that it will exemplify the program of historically-grounded inquiry into large-scale processes of change I have advocated in earlier books such as
Big Structures, Large Processes, Huge Comparisons
and
As Sociology Meets History,

and that it will contribute to the effort to work out theories of historical contingency exemplified by recent writings of Anthony Giddens, Allan Pred, Arthur Stinchcombe, and Harrison White. If so, compulsion and phobia will once again have made a constructive contribution to knowledge. Now, of course, I face a problem: that big book still awaits me.
